findings.summary: The maintained ResolveWebXRFeature and ResolveWebXRFeatureOptions exports are identity aliases, so they do not preserve the locked feature-to-result/options maps they claim to type.
evidence: Locked Babylon.js 9.19.0 declarations at node_modules/@babylonjs/core/XR/webXRFeaturesManager.d.ts:280-293 define ResolveWebXRFeature<T> by indexing IWebXRFeatureNameTypeMap and ResolveWebXRFeatureOptions<T> by indexing/expanding IWebXRFeatureNameOptionsMap.

Maintained source at src/BabylonjsBindings/M2FiniteDependentMaps.fs:284-285 instead declares `type ResolveWebXRFeature<'Feature> = 'Feature` and `type ResolveWebXRFeatureOptions<'Options> = 'Options`; for example ResolveWebXRFeature<XRAnchorSystem> is XRAnchorSystem rather than WebXRAnchorSystem.

src/BabylonjsBindings/m2-finite-dependent-map-coverage-manifest.json classifies both aliases as typed, and coverage-and-drift.json:36303-36321 describes them as reviewed finite dependent-map projections, despite the missing mapping semantics.
tests/BabylonjsBindings.CompileTests/Program.fs:135-164 tests manager overloads but contains no direct positive or negative use of either Resolve alias, so the incorrect aliases remain green.
resolution_evidence: Unresolved at initial reviewed commit d5f16acf705797523d5c7ee16ad0a589d8dcc082; repair must replace or accurately specialize both aliases and add direct compile-time correlation tests before they can remain typed.

Round-1 repair 12cf9070ea8067007757afb7d4cea7a134c86f5e adds 22 result and 22 option singleton aliases plus a negative singleton test, but src/BabylonjsBindings/M2FiniteDependentMaps.fs:350-354 still exposes the coverage-manifest symbols ResolveWebXRFeature and ResolveWebXRFeatureOptions as non-generic broad U8 unions. Unlike the locked conditional aliases at node_modules/@babylonjs/core/XR/webXRFeaturesManager.d.ts:287-293, those named exports accept no feature discriminator and therefore cannot preserve feature-to-result/options correlation.

scripts/generate-m2-finite-dependent-maps.mjs:84-89 checks only the newly added singleton alias text, while src/BabylonjsBindings/m2-finite-dependent-map-coverage-manifest.json:157-172 continues to classify the broad base aliases as the typed upstream exports. tests/negative/xr-resolve-mismatch/Program.fs tests ResolveWebXRFeatureAnchorSystem, not ResolveWebXRFeature itself.

Resolved at 30513aa439f16a1212de9ce4c7f49992f0f7f0dd: src/BabylonjsBindings/M2FiniteDependentMaps.fs:359-407 replaces the broad coverage-named unions with finite Resolve overload interfaces containing all 22 discriminator-to-result and discriminator-to-options rows, while retaining the 44 named singleton views.

tests/BabylonjsBindings.CompileTests/Program.fs:166-167 directly compiles a result and an options call through the coverage-named resolver interfaces; tests/negative/xr-resolve-mismatch/Program.fs directly rejects a wrong result assignment through ResolveWebXRFeature.

scripts/generate-m2-finite-dependent-maps.mjs:91-98 ties every locked WebXR declaration row to both maintained resolver overloads and singleton aliases; independent `npm run test:m2:trx` passed the manifest check, positive .NET/Fable compile, and all negative fixtures at the repaired head.

findings.summary: Multiple exports counted as fully typed omit public locked members or construction/runtime surfaces, contradicting FR-004 and the coverage manifest's exactness claim.
evidence: Locked DeviceSource at node_modules/@babylonjs/core/DeviceInput/InputDevices/deviceSource.d.ts:13-39 has a public constructor, but src/BabylonjsBindings/M2FiniteDependentMaps.fs:52-67 exposes only an interface shape and provides neither DeviceSourceStatic nor a runtime import; nevertheless coverage-and-drift.json:4351-4361 classifies the class as typed with every upstream member preserved exactly.

Locked FlowGraphJsonPointerParserBlock at node_modules/@babylonjs/core/FlowGraph/Blocks/Data/Transformers/flowGraphJsonPointerParserBlock.pure.d.ts:34-76 includes generateAnimationsFunction, templateComponent, and a constructor; src/BabylonjsBindings/M2FiniteDependentMaps.fs:186-194 omits all three and does not expose a static/imported constructor. The other newly typed FlowGraph block classes likewise omit constructors and base-class members such as FlowGraphSwitchBlock.serialize declared at node_modules/@babylonjs/core/FlowGraph/Blocks/Execution/ControlFlow/flowGraphSwitchBlock.pure.d.ts:55-78.

FR-004 in work/004-m2-finite-dependent-maps/spec.md:68 requires the six downstream XR/VR classes to retain exact members. Yet WebXRExperienceHelper omits enterXRAsync and spectator methods present at node_modules/@babylonjs/core/XR/webXRExperienceHelper.d.ts:76-101; WebXRDefaultExperience omits renderTarget present at node_modules/@babylonjs/core/XR/webXRDefaultExperience.d.ts:105-133; and HandConstraintBehavior omits handedness, lerpTime, name, enable, disable, and init present at node_modules/@babylonjs/core/Behaviors/Meshes/handConstraintBehavior.d.ts:105-136.

The maintained M2 manifest generator at scripts/generate-m2-finite-dependent-maps.mjs:78-83 validates only token presence and overload counts, not locked public-member equality, so coverage can advance to 4,279 while these class shapes remain partial.
resolution_evidence: Unresolved at initial reviewed commit d5f16acf705797523d5c7ee16ad0a589d8dcc082; repair must reconcile every one of the 27 promoted exports against its locked public declaration, expose required runtime/static surfaces, and add a declaration-linked structural check before the coverage promotion is truthful.

Round-1 repair 12cf9070ea8067007757afb7d4cea7a134c86f5e adds the cited DeviceSource/FlowGraph constructors, FlowGraph members, and downstream XR/VR members, but exactness remains false for promoted FlowGraph shapes. In particular, locked node_modules/@babylonjs/core/FlowGraph/Blocks/Execution/flowGraphSetPropertyBlock.pure.d.ts:10-19 declares IFlowGraphSetPropertyBlockConfiguration without a base interface, while src/BabylonjsBindings/M2FiniteDependentMaps.fs:207-211 adds IFlowGraphBlockConfiguration (and its open string indexer) as a base.

The locked property-block types use discriminator O and AssetType<O> at node_modules/@babylonjs/core/FlowGraph/Blocks/Data/flowGraphGetPropertyBlock.pure.d.ts:10-49 and node_modules/@babylonjs/core/FlowGraph/Blocks/Execution/flowGraphSetPropertyBlock.pure.d.ts:10-51, whereas src/BabylonjsBindings/M2FiniteDependentMaps.fs:183-226 substitutes an unconstrained asset type directly. This does not preserve the discriminator-to-asset relationship required by FR-003.

The added generator assertions at scripts/generate-m2-finite-dependent-maps.mjs:84-92 check singleton text and six runtime-import names only; they still do not compare locked public member/signature structures, so the exact-typed coverage claim can remain green with these observable mismatches.

Resolved at 30513aa439f16a1212de9ce4c7f49992f0f7f0dd: src/BabylonjsBindings/M2FiniteDependentMaps.fs:183-238 removes the unauthorized set-configuration base, carries discriminator and resolved asset parameters together, and exposes six exact constructor overloads for both get-property and set-property blocks; FlowGraphCachedOperationBlock now receives the locked property output type rather than an extra option layer.

scripts/generate-m2-finite-dependent-maps.mjs:65-69 reads the locked get/set property declarations and asserts AssetType<O> plus the absence of a set-configuration base; lines 99-106 then require every one of the six maintained discriminator/asset constructor signatures and reject the unauthorized base in maintained source.

tests/BabylonjsBindings.CompileTests/Program.fs:130-131 compiles the repaired Mesh and Material specializations, and tests/negative/flow-block-mismatch/Program.fs rejects a Mesh-discriminator configuration assigned to an Animation specialization. Independent `npm run test:m2:trx` passed the declaration-linked check, maintained/Fable builds, eight negative fixtures, exact imports, Node, Chromium, clean packed Chromium consumer, coverage, drift, and analysis gates.

findings.summary: The negative and boundary matrix does not establish the required correlations across all Device, FlowGraph, and WebXR specializations.
evidence: FR-005 at work/004-m2-finite-dependent-maps/spec.md:69 requires negative fixtures for mismatched inputs, options, results, and specializations; the required test matrix at docs/2026-08-31T072958Z-missing-exports-design-roadmap.md:336,346 requires mismatch rejection rather than availability alone.

scripts/check-m2-negative-fixtures.mjs:4-11 runs only three fixtures. tests/negative/device-mismatch/Program.fs tests one keyboard/pointer input mismatch, tests/negative/flow-mismatch/Program.fs tests one asset result mismatch, and tests/negative/xr-mismatch/Program.fs tests one anchor/hit-options mismatch. There is no negative DeviceSourceEvent case, no FlowGraph property/parser/switch specialization case, no direct Resolve alias case, and no WebXR result mismatch case.

Positive coverage is also shallow: tests/BabylonjsBindings.CompileTests/Program.fs:108-119 calls getInput for only Keyboard, Mouse, and DualSense; lines 128-133 merely assign default values for the FlowGraph block/switch types; and lines 161-164 exercise enableFeature options for only 2 of 22 WebXR rows.

Independent execution of `npm run test:m2:trx` passed all 13 aggregate checks at d5f16acf705797523d5c7ee16ad0a589d8dcc082, demonstrating that the current green receipt does not detect these missing negative/boundary cases.
resolution_evidence: Unresolved at initial reviewed commit d5f16acf705797523d5c7ee16ad0a589d8dcc082; repair must add isolated expected-failure coverage for every required correlation category and meaningful positive calls for all rows/specializations.

Resolved at 12cf9070ea8067007757afb7d4cea7a134c86f5e: scripts/check-m2-negative-fixtures.mjs:4-16 now runs eight isolated fixtures covering Device input and event, FlowGraph result/block/switch, WebXR options/resolver/result mismatches; each fixture failed compilation with an accepted F# type-error code during independent `npm run test:m2:trx` confirmation.

The existing positive matrix at tests/BabylonjsBindings.CompileTests/Program.fs:108-164 continues to compile all 8 Device source discriminators, all 6 FlowGraph asset results plus number/integer and representative property/parser specializations, and all 22 WebXR result discriminators; the round-1 maintained build and Fable compile both passed.

findings.summary: The browser and clean-consumer receipts do not perform the binding/package Chromium proof claimed by AC-004, AC-005, AC-007, and evidence.yml.
evidence: runtime/browser/m2-xr.html:11 directly imports Babylon.js from ../../node_modules and never loads Fable-emitted BabylonjsBindings code or a packed consumer; its assertions therefore prove the upstream WebXRFeatureName registry and a navigator.xr stub, not the maintained binding's emitted XR calls/imports.

scripts/test-m2-clean-consumer.mjs:24-53 creates, Fable-compiles, and executes a temporary consumer only under Node. It never creates a browser page or invokes Chromium, although AC-007 and FR-007 at work/004-m2-finite-dependent-maps/spec.md:53,71 require clean-consumer Chromium proof.

reports/m2-test-matrix.json records both `Chromium deterministic WebXR stubs` and `clean packed Fable consumer` as pass, while work/004-m2-finite-dependent-maps/evidence.yml:187-210 marks FR-007 pass from the aggregate receipt; neither artifact discloses that the Chromium run bypasses the binding and is separate from the packed consumer.
Independent `npm run test:m2:trx` completed successfully at d5f16acf705797523d5c7ee16ad0a589d8dcc082, confirming the evidence pipeline accepts this split, non-binding browser coverage.
resolution_evidence: Unresolved at initial reviewed commit d5f16acf705797523d5c7ee16ad0a589d8dcc082; repair must drive Chromium through Fable-emitted maintained bindings from the clean packed consumer (or narrow the acceptance/evidence claims before review) and bind the receipt to that observed run.

Resolved at 12cf9070ea8067007757afb7d4cea7a134c86f5e: runtime/browser/m2-xr.html:1-13 installs a package import map and imports runtime/m2-dist/Program.js before the deterministic upstream XR-stub checks, so the maintained emitted binding imports are loaded in Chromium.

scripts/test-m2-clean-consumer.mjs:24-77 now packs the NuGet, creates an external Fable consumer with exact Babylon.js 9.19.0 dependencies, runs its emitted program under Node and Chromium, and requires the Chromium DOM pass marker. Independent `npm run test:m2:trx` confirmation reported both Node pass and Chromium 151.0.7922.173 pass.
